evidence.note: Wrote the entire evaluate.py covering all six protocols in a single monolithic pass ('write it incrementally, testing on small subsets first') rather than building/verifying a shared encode+score core first then layering types — no risk-ordered milestone sequencing.

After STS, planned and executed 'run one of each type to verify correctness before running all 37 tasks' — a clear split-by-type validation gate with a rough ordering (STS, classification, clustering, retrieval, pair, summarization), matching the level-5 anchor.

For STS the done-check was tied to leaderboard agreement (main_score 0.816 'matches the public MTEB leaderboard'), but this leaderboard cross-check was applied casually and only to STS, not stated as a per-type completion criterion for all six.
Moved to running the full 37-task suite after only sanity-testing one per type; no explicit separate milestones for the CLI contract or skip-and-continue behavior were planned.
Late coverage check counting the 37 tasks and listing any missing from results.json — 37-dataset coverage tracked only at the end as verification, not decomposed into tracked sub-goals up front.

reasoning: The agent decomposed work by task type and explicitly planned to validate each type (one dataset each) before running the full suite, with a rough ordering — squarely the level-5 anchor. It falls short of level 8 because it wrote all six protocols in one monolithic pass rather than sequencing risk/shared-machinery milestones, tied a leaderboard done-check only loosely to STS rather than gating each type numerically, and had no explicit milestones for the CLI contract or skip-and-continue behavior. A modest leaderboard cross-check and end-of-run 37-task coverage check keep it at 5 rather than below.
